static_traits.name: Chen Kai
static_traits.social_status: Keeps distance from friends and family; has a few friends to talk with, but has not shared the extent of their despair
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; has not experienced similar psychological problems; has not received psychotherapy
static_traits.language_features: Neutral attitude; clear expression, fairly coherent logic; able to cooperate with counseling exploration

basic_info.main_problem: I feel despair and hopelessness about future job prospects; after completing my master's degree I could not enter my ideal field and worry I will be unemployed forever. The distress began after graduation, occurs almost daily, and worsens when I see peers succeeding in their careers.
basic_info.core_demands: 'I want to find a way to feel less trapped.'
growth_experiences: After completing a master's degree and entering the job-seeking stage, the client long faced rejection and frustration at not entering the ideal field; when seeing peers succeed professionally, the client felt 'left behind', and self-esteem was affected; the client gradually distanced from friends and family, with reduced motivation and changes in eating habits.

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not get a job in the ideal field, it means I am inferior to them and am a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Distances from friends and family to avoid comparison and evaluation; increases job-seeking and social networking attempts
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am behind; I am not as good as them; I may never find a suitable job

special_situations.event: After completing a master's degree, repeatedly rejected in job hunting
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If rejected many times, it proves I have no ability and the future is doomed to failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly polishing resume and interview skills, but at the same time constantly ruminating on negative outcomes
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: These rejections mean I will be unemployed forever

special_situations.event: Getting several interviews but no offer
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only getting hired counts as success; a smooth interview does not count as positive evidence
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Discounting positive performance, ignoring one's own progress
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Performing well in the interview is useless; it shows I am still not good enough

special_situations.event: Currently not working in the ideal field
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If not working in the ideal field, it equals failure, and one's whole life will be trapped in a disliked job
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Presuming the worst outcome in an extreme way, repeatedly worrying in order to seek control
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will keep doing the job I hate forever; it is meaningless

core_conflict.wish: Longs to engage in meaningful work matching own expertise, gaining recognition and a sense of self-worth
core_conflict.fear: Fears failure and rejection, fears appearing inferior to others when compared with peers, and ultimately living a meaningless life
defense_goal: Reducing shame and anxiety through detachment and disqualifying positive evidence
Using catastrophic expectations to avoid the disappointment brought by uncertainty

object_relations.self_representation: A lagging, failed job seeker (a not-good-enough self)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor or others point out positive signs in job seeking (such as obtaining an interview)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client believes these do not count, and only receiving an offer has value (transference: regarding positive feedback as invalid)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Uses negative language, emphasizing 'meaningless / does not count', with a flat, somewhat negative tone, downplaying positive evidence.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When seeing peers share career success or hearing others have been hired
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client compares in an extreme manner, viewing themselves as 'completely behind' and others as 'completely successful' (transference: splitting cognition)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Uses absolute words (such as 'forever, always, completely'), reinforces self-negation, and avoids discussing intermediate possibilities.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When alone or reflecting on the future after experiencing multiple job rejections
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Internalizes external rejection as a wholesale negation of self-worth (transference: absorbing others' judgments as one's own voice)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: States 'I am not good enough' in a self-critical tone, reducing emotional expression and stating more conclusions.

manifestations: Worrying about 'doing a job I hate for a lifetime, never finding a matching position'
Believing years of study were wasted
Distancing from friends and family due to low self-esteem
Reduced contact with the support system
outcomes: Further decline in sense of self-worth

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact
manifestations: When positive progress is pointed out (such as having an interview), shifts instead to emphasizing the negative conclusion 'it is meaningless'
When talking about the future, quickly jumping to the worst-case scenario, avoiding detailing realistic possibilities

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths
manifestations: Using 'only getting hired counts as success' as an absolute standard
Treating employer and others' expectations as the only basis for measuring self-worth

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact
manifestations: 频繁Self-denial与贬低成就
Reduces contact with friends and family out of feeling 'undeserving'

exception_events.target_problem: In the job-seeking process, the client usually ignores positive signs due to despair and self-negation, and makes catastrophic predictions about the future, leading to reduced motivation.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In several interviews, the client performed well and gained from the process an understanding of employers' needs and interview experience. Unlike before, these moments showed potential that can be recognized by employers.
exception_events.reason: Different approach: continuously engaged in job seeking and interview practice; different understanding: gradually learned employers' concerns and job requirements, thereby improving interview skills.

positive_force: Performance in interviews has improved; gradually understanding employers' needs
Continues job hunting and networking; has not completely given up
Has some social support (has a few friends to talk with)
negative_force: Marked cognitive biases such as catastrophizing and black-and-white thinking
Excessive comparison with peers, reinforcing inferiority and shame
Discounting positive evidence, filtering out positive information
Self-worth overly tied to career achievement, leading to frustrated motivation and emotions
Social avoidance reduces support and worsens mood

target_behavior.behavior: Catastrophic expectations about future employment and all-or-nothing thinking
antecedent: Repeated job rejections after completing a master's degree
Currently not working in the ideal field
target_behavior.core_reason: Highly binds self-worth to whether they receive an offer in the ideal field, introjecting the external standard that one 'must succeed'
target_behavior.function: Attempts to reduce the anxiety and potential disappointment brought by uncertainty by presuming the worst outcome (avoiding emotions)
target_behavior.consequence: Persistent despair and anxiety reduce job-search motivation and engagement in life

antecedent: Seeing news of the success of others
target_behavior.core_reason: Shame and comparison lead to fear of being judged
target_behavior.function: Avoids others' evaluations and comparisons for short-term relief of anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Social support decreases, loneliness increases, and mood worsens further

target_behavior.behavior: Reduced activity and low motivation (including changes in eating habits)
target_behavior.core_reason: Believes effort is meaningless; falls into hopelessness and self-negation
target_behavior.function: Avoiding investing in tasks that might fail, reducing stress and energy consumption in the short term
target_behavior.consequence: Quality of life declines, physical and mental state suffers, job-search efficiency drops
